example: "Because page." beside "Ada unfolds the page so Ben can check it"
if_many: Repair: Rehearse the answer with a subject and predicate. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: Spells a studied word by an unrelated sound pattern.
shows: A child writes or says: "sed for said"
example: "sed for said" beside "said, because, sitting, smiled, cries, happiness"
if_many: Repair: Map its spoken sounds to the studied spelling. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: Adds a suffix without the required base change.
shows: A child writes or says: "siting for sitting"
example: "siting for sitting" beside "said, because, sitting, smiled, cries, happiness"
if_many: Repair: Compare the base with the doubled, dropped-e or changed-y form. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: Divides a long word so a syllable cannot be blended.
shows: A child writes or says: "Splits the word so no chunk can be blended."
example: "Splits the word so no chunk can be blended." beside "Reads each chunk and blends the word: invitation, sudden, covered"
if_many: Repair: Mark known vowel patterns and redivide before blending. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: Regularizes an irregular word while reading.
shows: A child writes or says: "sayd for said"
example: "sayd for said" beside "All four are read with their usual sounds: said as sed, does as duz, were as wur, their"
if_many: Repair: Map its unexpected letters to the spoken word, then reread. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: Keeps extended writing but no short writing record.
shows: A child writes or says: "Only the review is shown, with no short writing in the folder."
example: "Only the review is shown, with no short writing in the folder." beside "The notes were for myself, the story for a partner, the recommendation for a classmate"
if_many: Repair: Recover dated brief responses alongside the extended draft. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: Omits speech punctuation around dialogue.
shows: A child writes or says: "Ben said Let us try."
example: "Ben said Let us try." beside ""Could you check this?" Ada asked"
if_many: Repair: Mark the spoken words, then place quotation marks and the reporting comma. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: Capitalizes small words in a title.
shows: A child writes or says: "A Series For Every Reader"
example: "A Series For Every Reader" beside "A Series for Every Reader"
if_many: Repair: Compare with the title model and lowercase for, of, and, the unless first. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: Speaks a report so fast the listener cannot follow.
shows: A child writes or says: "Rushes through the report until the listeners cannot follow."
example: "Rushes through the report until the listeners cannot follow." beside "Explains Ada's changed action with facts, a descriptive detail and an understandable pace"
if_many: Repair: Mark pause points between facts and rehearse once for the listener. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: Adds an unstated fact as textual evidence.
shows: Locate the supporting sentence, or say the text does not answer.
example: Wrong: "Farms use more water than zoos." Right: "The card says the farm pipes water to the fields."
if_many: 7 minutes, children point to the sentence in a card and say The text says ... so ... for three questions, one of which the text does not answer.

error: Names a small detail as the main idea.
shows: Test a sentence that covers the whole passage.
example: Wrong: "The main idea is the pools." Right: "A zoo needs water for animals and cleaning."
if_many: 6 minutes, test does this fit every line on three candidate lines.

error: Lists details without explaining support.
shows: Join one detail to the main idea with because.
example: Wrong: "The farm has crops. The zoo has pools." Right: "Both places need water because animals and work need it."
if_many: 8 minutes, add because to each detail on a slip and pair slips to the main idea.

error: Uses a familiar dictionary meaning that conflicts with context.
shows: Test meanings in the complete sentence.
example: Wrong: current as the time now. Right: moving water in a creek.
if_many: 6 minutes, read the whole sentence with each meaning and keep the one that fits.

error: Reverses a temporal relationship.
shows: Trace the printed arrows before choosing before or after.
example: Wrong: "The gutter comes after the barrel." Right: "The arrow goes gutter, barrel, tap."
if_many: 5 minutes, finger-trace the arrows on a fresh diagram and say first, next, last.

error: Compares only similarities or only differences.
shows: Use paired rows for shared and distinct points and details.
example: Wrong: "The account is about Kenya and the town text is about a plant." Right: "Both say clean water must reach people."
if_many: 6 minutes, write a shared point first on each pair of cards, then the differences.

error: Labels a word class without explaining its function.
shows: Say what the word does in this sentence.
example: Wrong: "slowly is an adverb." Right: "slowly tells how the workers inspect."
if_many: 6 minutes, each child says the job aloud before the name of the word class.

error: Uses a verb form that disagrees with its subject.
shows: Match singular or plural subject to the verb.
example: Wrong: "The workers inspects." Right: "The workers inspect; the worker inspects."
if_many: 6 minutes, find the subject, say singular or plural, match the verb.

error: Uses a pronoun that disagrees with its intended referent.
shows: Draw a reference arrow and match number.
example: Wrong: "It" for plural nouns. Right: "They" for plural nouns, "it" for one thing.
if_many: 6 minutes, draw an arrow from the pronoun back to its noun.

error: Attributes the reader's judgment to the author.
shows: Label whose judgment each sentence states.
example: Wrong: "The writer says we should explain the pond first." Right: "I say pond first. The writer says both jobs."
if_many: 7 minutes, label each sentence writer or me with two colours.

error: Treats a nonliteral phrase as a physical action.
shows: Test both readings against the surrounding events.
example: Wrong: "Staff put an eye on the gauge." Right: "Staff watch the gauge carefully."
if_many: 6 minutes, test both readings against the next sentence.

error: Gives a topic without an opinion.
shows: Add the choice the essay will defend.
example: Wrong: "Fuel and water." Right: "Our class should explain stopping fuel first."
if_many: Written move with the 145 feedback, used in the first five minutes of 146.

error: Supports an opinion only with personal liking.
shows: Replace liking with a source-based reason.
example: Wrong: "I like lids." Right: "A cracked lid lets dirt in."
if_many: Written move with the 145 feedback, used in the first five minutes of 146.

error: Uses a connector that misstates the relationship.
shows: Name the relationship before selecting its connector.
example: Wrong: "A cracked lid lets dirt in, but lid care comes first." Right: "... so lid care comes first."
if_many: Written move with the 145 feedback, used in the first five minutes of 146.

error: Ends without a relevant conclusion.
shows: Return to the piece's topic or position in a closing sentence.
example: Wrong: a paragraph that stops after the second reason. Right: "So a pond needs both jobs."
if_many: Written move with the 145 feedback, used in the first five minutes of 146.

error: Reports a preference as research learning.
shows: Name one sourced distinction learned through the inquiry.
example: Wrong: "I learned I like the access text best." Right: "I learned that reaching water and safe water are different."
if_many: Written move with the 145 feedback, used in the first five minutes of 146.

error: Copies a whole source instead of taking brief notes.
shows: Shorten one source fact into a few words.
example: Wrong: "A cap keeps dirt out of a well." Right: "cap keeps dirt out (Wells card)".
if_many: Written move with the 145 feedback, used in the first five minutes of 146.

error: Adds a regular plural ending where the noun has an irregular plural form.
shows: Retrieve the singular and its known irregular plural together.
example: Wrong: "gooses." Right: "one goose, two geese."
if_many: Written move with the 145 feedback, used in the first five minutes of 146.

error: Identifies an object as an abstract noun.
shows: Contrast a touchable object with a named idea.
example: Wrong: "A tank is an abstract noun." Right: "Patience names an idea."
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Treats clean recopying as revision.
shows: Show one meaning change responding to written feedback.
example: Wrong: the same draft written out again. Right: one reason changed after the feedback.
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Mixes unrelated information in one group.
shows: Sort facts by the named subtopic before arranging paragraphs.
example: Wrong: "Settling removes heavier particles. Buses leave at three." Right: both sentences about settling.
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Substitutes a vague claim for developed information.
shows: Add a definition and a specific source detail.
example: Wrong: "Water matters. It is important." Right: "In settling, heavier particles sink."
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Ignores what the reader needs for the purpose.
shows: Add the background this reader needs before the request.
example: Wrong: "Screens are great." Right: "A screen catches twigs so they stay out of the water."
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Offers one sitting as evidence of sustained writing.
shows: Locate the dated plan, draft and later revision in the folder.
example: Wrong: one paragraph written in a morning. Right: a dated plan, a draft and a later revision.
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Omits the comma between city and state.
shows: Mark the city-state boundary before editing the address.
example: Wrong: "Cedar Bay OR 97100". Right: "Cedar Bay, OR 97100".
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Rushes speech so the listener loses meaning.
shows: Phrase a source sentence at its meaning boundaries.
example: Wrong: a whole sentence said in one breath. Right: pauses at the meaning boundaries.
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Uses a fragment when clarification needs a complete sentence.
shows: Restate the clarification with a subject and verb.
example: Wrong: "Before there, stuff." Right: "The screen removes leaves before water enters storage."
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Speaks a written delivery cue as part of the message.
shows: Replace the written cue with the corresponding pause or emphasis.
example: Wrong: saying the words bracket pause aloud. Right: a real pause.
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Treats watching an adult type as individual digital production.
shows: Have the child type and revise an attributed contribution.
example: Wrong: an adult types while the child watches. Right: the child types a line and signs it.
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Relies on the teacher reading the passage to supply its meaning.
shows: Reread the hard part silently and name one strategy before asking for help.
example: Wrong: waiting for the teacher to read the hard line aloud. Right: rereading it and naming a strategy.
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 155.

error: Reports an isolated number as the listening main idea.
shows: State the change using both bars and the remaining-leak drawing.
example: Wrong: "Five." Right: "Some storage is ready, but two barrels remain empty."
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 156.

error: Enters discussion without studied evidence.
shows: Prepare one located passage before taking a turn.
example: Wrong: "I like it best." Right: "The second paragraph says why."
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 156.

error: Interrupts another speaker.
shows: Use the agreed signal to request the floor.
example: Wrong: talking over a peer. Right: raising the signal and waiting.
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 156.

error: Changes topic instead of linking to a peer.
shows: Begin with the peer's specific claim before responding.
example: Wrong: "I like swimming." Right: "You said litter can hurt a stream; what harm?"
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 156.

error: Repeats a first claim without considering the exchange.
shows: Explain what the other contribution changed or confirmed.
example: Wrong: saying the first claim again. Right: "After you said that, I see ..."
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 156.

error: Answers a request for detail with yes alone.
shows: Add the requested source and its relevant detail.
example: Wrong: "Yes." Right: "What kind of harm do you mean?"
if_many: Show this error beside the corrected response on 156.

error: Guesses a long word from its first letter.
shows: Read every syllable, blend, then confirm with context.
example: Wrong: reads evaporates as every. Right: eh-VAP-uh-rates, blended by syllable and confirmed by the sentence.
if_many: 8 minutes, scoop each syllable on three long words, then read each in a sentence.

error: Treats freshwater as automatically drinkable.
shows: Separate salt content from treatment and safety evidence.
example: Wrong: "Fresh water is safe to drink." Right: "Fresh means not salty; the sign says it may not be safe."
if_many: 7 minutes, sort six sentences into salt content and safe to drink.

error: Makes a story character's view the narrator's view.
shows: Label the speaker beside each judgment before comparing with your own.
example: Wrong: "Sam thinks sharing is kind, so the narrator does." Right: "Sam wants the biggest bucket; the narrator calls sharing kind."
if_many: 6 minutes, write the speaker's name beside each judgment before comparing.

error: Uses an illustration without its accompanying words.
shows: Combine a labelled visual detail with its text explanation.
example: Wrong: "The picture shows a tap." Right: "The picture shows the water path in order; the line only names the tap."
if_many: 8 minutes, label the picture, then add one word from the sentence.

error: Writes regular -s where -es is needed.
shows: Compare box and boxes before editing another regular plural.
example: Wrong: "dishs." Right: "dishes."
if_many: Written move with the 145 feedback, used in the first five minutes of 146; applied independently on 155.

error: Treats an invented episode as factual source evidence.
shows: Separate and label invented events before returning to factual notes.
example: Wrong: a note "Mina's well sang to her" filed under research. Right: the note is labelled invented and kept out of the notes.
if_many: 8 minutes, children label four lines fact or invented, then repair one note.

error: Files a brief note under the wrong research category.
shows: Match the note to the category question.
example: Wrong: a distance note filed under pollution. Right: the same note under access.
if_many: Written move with the 145 feedback: contrast a distance note under pollution with the same note under access, then sort another note in the first five minutes of 146.

error: Omits required doubling before a suffix.
shows: Contrast sit plus ing with sitting, then apply doubling to another taught base.
example: Wrong: "siting." Right: "sitting."
if_many: Written repair on 143.

error: Applies a regular sound pattern to an irregular word.
shows: Map the irregular spelling to its spoken form, then reread it in context.
example: Wrong: said read to rhyme with paid. Right: said read to rhyme with bed.
if_many: Written repair on 143.

error: Ignores known word-part meanings when deriving a word.
shows: Build the new meaning from the known base and added part.
example: Wrong: "unsafe means more safe." Right: "unsafe means not safe: un- reverses safe."
if_many: 6 minutes, build unsafe and unclear from the base and the part, then say the meaning of each aloud.

error: Contradicts a stated detail of the text.
shows: Reread the sentence that states it and correct the claim.
example: Wrong: "The writer wants one bucket for the rich." Right: "The article asks for a bucket for every house."
if_many: 5 minutes, reread the stating sentence and correct the claim.

error: Gives an answer from the reader's own life or ideas, not the text.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: An answer the words do not support.
if_many: Put a finger on the line that says it and read it back. 5 minutes, a group on day 80.

error: Names the topic, not a lesson or main idea.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "It is about a goat."
if_many: Say the whole idea in one sentence, then test it against two lines. 5 minutes.

error: Reads a nonliteral phrase as a physical event.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "His cheeks were on fire."
if_many: Say what the words would mean if real, then what they mean here. 5 minutes.

error: Names a trait with no action from the text beside it.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "Tobin was stubborn."
if_many: Add "so he" and finish with what the character did. 5 minutes.

error: Gives a detail the text does not say, or one that does not support the point.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: A detail from outside the text.
if_many: Find the line first, then say what it shows. 5 minutes.

error: Describes the picture but not what it adds to the words.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "There is a hen."
if_many: Ask what the picture shows that the words leave out. 5 minutes.

error: Answers without the words from the text that support it.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: An answer with no copied words.
if_many: Find and copy the words, then say them again. 5 minutes.

error: Puts events out of order, or reverses cause and effect.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: The last step first.
if_many: Number the steps on cards, then read them with first, next, last. 5 minutes.

error: Names a signal word but not what it links.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "Because." and nothing more.
if_many: Say what comes before the word and what comes after. 5 minutes.

error: Chooses a heading, page or number by guess, not by the question.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: The wrong heading.
if_many: Say the question, find its key word, then look. 5 minutes.

error: Gives a search trail with no keyword, or a link with no reason.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "Click the link."
if_many: Pick the word from the question, then say why the link fits. 5 minutes.

error: Gives a word meaning from outside, ignoring the sentence around it.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: A meaning that does not fit.
if_many: Read the sentence with the meaning in place. 5 minutes.

error: A paragraph has facts but no topic sentence.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: Facts only.
if_many: Write one sentence that says what the box is. 5 minutes, then the revision part.

error: Facts are in the order given, not grouped.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: A list of facts.
if_many: Sort the strips into two piles, then write each pile. 5 minutes.

error: Names things but gives no fact, definition or detail.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "A box."
if_many: Add one fact that tells more. 5 minutes.

error: Ideas are not linked, or one link word does all the work.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "and and and"
if_many: Choose a different link word for each pair. 5 minutes.

error: The paragraph stops with no closing, or a closing about something else.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "I like dogs."
if_many: Say what the facts show, then write it. 5 minutes.

error: Guesses a word from its first letters.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: Says a different word with the same start.
if_many: Cover the first letter; touch each part, then blend. 5 minutes.

error: Drops or misreads a prefix or suffix.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: Says the base word only.
if_many: Mark the base, then the ending, then read the whole word. 5 minutes.

error: Gives the meaning of a different prefix or suffix, or none.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: Says re- means not.
if_many: Match the part to its meaning card. 5 minutes.

error: Sounds out an irregular word letter by letter.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: Reads heart as hurt.
if_many: Star the unusual part and say the word whole. 5 minutes.

error: Reads word by word with no phrasing.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: Each word at one pitch.
if_many: Echo a line in phrases, then read it. 5 minutes.

error: Leaves a misread and goes on.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: Says close with a z sound and goes on.
if_many: Read the sentence, ask "does it make sense?", reread. 5 minutes.

error: Gives a liking or a story from home as the purpose.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "I have a tent at home."
if_many: Look at the title; finish "I want to find out ___." 5 minutes.

error: Reads the words but cannot say what they told.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: Silence after reading.
if_many: Read one sentence, say it in your own words, then the next. 5 minutes.

error: Gives a fact as the writer's view, or the writer's view as the reader's own.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: A fact sentence copied for the writer's view.
if_many: Name fact and view with two colours, then match each to the writer or the reader. 5 minutes.

error: Compares from one article only, or gives a likeness where a difference was asked.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "The tent is cool."
if_many: Two columns, one for each article; mark what appears in both. 5 minutes.

error: Accepts a faulty comparison, or fixes it with a new fault.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "Nothing is wrong."
if_many: Check each part of the sentence against each article, one part at a time. 5 minutes.

error: Gives a liking or a reason that is not in the articles.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "I like the walk."
if_many: Find the line in an article for each reason before writing it. 5 minutes.

error: States no opinion, or lists facts without saying what to choose.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "The Story Walk has pages. The tent has pillows."
if_many: Finish "I think the school should use ___ because ___." 5 minutes.

error: Ends on a last reason or a different idea instead of a closing.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "The tent is open on weekends."
if_many: Write a last sentence that begins "That is why". 5 minutes.

error: Forms a plural, tense, verb or agreement wrongly.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "The childs carried the boxs."
if_many: Say the sentence aloud, then fix the one word that sounds wrong. 5 minutes.

error: Names a word's job wrongly, or uses a joining word or sentence kind wrongly.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "The shelf is big and because it is red."
if_many: Match each joining word to the job it does, with one sentence each. 5 minutes.

error: Uses more or most where an ending fits, or swaps the two forms.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "more tall, most fast"
if_many: Compare two things, then three, and add -er then -est. 5 minutes.

error: Leaves out a capital, comma or quotation mark.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "Pip said I found it."
if_many: Mark the spoken words, then the commas, then the capitals. 5 minutes.

error: Leaves out the apostrophe or puts it in the wrong place.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "the boys hats"
if_many: Say who owns it, then add the apostrophe after the owner. 5 minutes.

error: Leaves a spelling mistake, or misapplies a spelling rule or the guide words.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "stoped, hopped"
if_many: Check the word against the rule, then the dictionary page. 5 minutes.

error: Names a chapter, scene or stanza but does not say how it builds on the one before.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "Rob frowns."
if_many: Say what the first part shows, then what the next part adds. 5 minutes.

error: Mixes up the narrator's, a character's and the reader's view.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "I think Rob is shy."
if_many: Ask three questions: who says it, who knows it, who thinks it. 5 minutes.

error: Compares only one story, or gives no likeness or no difference.
shows: Seen on the course check.
example: "The porch."
if_many: Two columns for the two stories; mark what is in both. 5 minutes.
